# Changelog

Versions here are the versions of the crates in this repository. Seven of
them go to crates.io, **out** together in dependency order:
`x0k-fact-projection`, `x0k-icon`, `x0k-ontology`, `x0k-syntax` first,
then `x0k-folio`, then `x0k-folio-ingest`, and `x0k-tangle` last. Each
upload resolves the ones beneath it against the live index, so the order
is not a convention — it is the only order that works. Two never reach
the registry: `x0k-folio-dialog` depends on `dialog-artifacts` by git
revision, which crates.io refuses, and `x0k-folio-cli` depends on it.
Both ship as the release binaries the npm wrapper installs, and both
build from a clone.

They do not all carry the same number. A crate's version moves when that
crate's own public surface moves, so a release names a subset of the bundle
and the rest keep the number they already have; the sections under a release
below are exactly the crates whose numbers moved in it. Reading a crate's
version as "how recent is this bundle" will mislead you — read the release
it is listed under instead.

## 0.1.1 — not yet published

The registry still serves 0.1.0, so `cargo install x0k-tangle` installs
0.1.0 until this release goes out. Building from a clone of this
repository gets you everything below today.

### x0k-fact-projection

- The envelope is spelled once. `envelope_predicates` is the single
  definition both projectors read, and it names the terms `document.ttl`
  declares — `x0k:status`, `x0k:docType`, `x0k:subtype`, `x0k:bodyFormat`,
  `x0k:concerns` (the constant `CONCERN` is now `CONCERNS`), plus `SUMMARY`
  and `ORIGINAL_ID`. Only provenance keeps the `folio/` prefix. A store
  filled under the old spelling is re-framed by a re-read of its documents,
  not refolded: clear the ingester's state file and ingest again. This is
  the API change the version bump is for.

### x0k-folio

- `check` validates typed declarations in **every namespace the loaded
  vocabulary declares**, not only `x0k:`. A module of your own — one that
  declares its own namespace with `vann:preferredNamespaceUri` — now has
  its instances checked the same way ours are. This is the API change the
  version bump is for: `check_instances` is public, and
  `DeclarationReport` carries what it found in one `defects` list.
- A refusal names what the loaded vocabulary actually admits, instead of
  what it does not; for a module file whose filename and declared
  namespace disagree, it names the rename that fixes the file.
- A rejected declaration block is reported at its line in your document,
  not as the name of a Rust struct.
- A declaration block whose fence marker and `id` disagree only in case —
  `yaml paper:Paper` over a `paper:paper/…` id — is told which spelling to
  use, rather than only that the two must agree.
- A marker a caller did not ask for is no longer a warning. Checking a set
  that declares icons printed one `WARN` per icon, on the first command
  the guide gives a new reader, about documents that were correct.

### x0k-tangle

- **A mirrored body containing a fenced block no longer grows the document
  on every `sync`.** `sync` wrote a three-backtick fence around whatever the
  source held, so a symbol whose own documentation carries a fenced example —
  how Python documents a public class — closed the chunk early, and the next
  run read the prose after it as part of the body and wrote that back too.
  Three syncs took one document from 21 lines to 35, and `check` could never
  go green again. The writer now picks a fence wide enough for the body it is
  about to write and ends the old body where a reader would end it, so the
  two agree by construction. **If you ran an earlier build over such a
  document, one `sync` repairs it** — the same command, and idempotent after.
  Three tests carry the shape that bit us:
  `a_mirror_whose_body_holds_a_fence_syncs_once`,
  `a_body_that_would_close_the_fence_widens_it`,
  `a_fence_ends_only_where_the_reader_ends_it`.
- `check`'s summary line counts what *failed*. It prints on a failing run,
  where it used to be written only for the passing one: over seven mirrors
  with one broken, the last line a reader met read `7 from= source references
  resolve` while the exit code said 1. It now reads `6 of 7`.
- `check` counts the Markdown it walked past — `1 markdown file carried no
  envelope` — and **`--require-envelope`** makes such a file a defect, for a
  set where every file is supposed to be typed. Skipping them is what lets
  adoption be incremental; not saying so is what leaves a generated board one
  row short.
- `tangle` prints its destinations relative to the workspace root, so both
  halves of `docs/ratelimit.md → crates/ratelimit/src/bucket.rs` are paths
  the reader can act on.
- `index` reads the envelope with the YAML parser `check` and `ingest` read
  it with, instead of a line scan. A flow sequence under `edges:`
  (`refined_by: [x0k:design/block]`) was silently dropped and a quoted scalar
  kept its quotes, so `index` and `check` described the same document
  differently. It still refuses nothing: a `type` or `status` no vocabulary
  declares is carried as written.
- **`check --closed` promotes a dangling edge from a note to a defect.**
  Without it an edge whose target is not under the paths scanned is a
  note and the run still exits 0, which is right for a collection that is
  part of something larger and wrong for one that is the whole world its
  edges name. Say `--closed` and the same finding exits 1, so a rename
  nobody finished fails CI. It covers declaration-block edges as well as
  envelope edges. Pass the whole set: over a subset, the edges into the
  rest of your own tree are the ones it reports.
- `index` records a document's title as a reader would say it, and carries
  the document's `summary` on the same record. A heading that is not the
  first thing in the body is a section name, not the page's name, and is
  no longer taken as a title; a document that names itself nowhere falls
  back to its `summary`, then to its filename.

### x0k-folio-cli

- **`query --named <question>` answers four canned questions with no query
  file**: `status` (every typed document with its status and path),
  `superseded` (each dead decision and what replaced it), `edges` and
  `mentions` (what a document points at, and what points at it — both take
  `--arg <id>`). The four are the questions a decision log is kept to
  answer, and none of them now costs a hand-written query.
- `--explain` prints the request a canned question would have run, so the
  question is also a worked example of what the query surface takes — and
  `--file` reads that output back unedited, envelope and all, which is what
  makes it a worked example rather than a picture of one.
- **`--arg` expands a compact id through your own vocabulary.** The prefix
  a reader writes is the one their module declared, so
  `--arg mycorp:design/x` finds `mycorp`'s document instead of asking about
  one in ours; a prefix no loaded vocabulary declares is refused and names
  what is declared, and an answer of nothing says whether it was the
  document or the edge that was missing.
- **`--named status` lists every typed document**, including the ones with
  no `status:` yet — the untriaged decisions are the ones an index page is
  kept for, and the board used to drop them silently.
- **`--named edges` and `--named mentions` ask over the predicates your
  vocabulary declares**, not only the ones this build compiled, and label
  each row the way your envelope spells it.
- **`ingest` defaults to the shipped vocabulary.** Forgetting the flag used
  to reject every document with an `edges:` block and leave a partly filled
  store behind an exit code. `--vocabulary <dir>` now reads your modules
  *in addition to* the shipped set — `--only-vocabulary` reads yours alone
  — so a module of your own no longer costs you the envelope's own terms.
  `x0k-tangle check --vocabulary` changed the same way, and the two verbs
  now load through one function, so a document one accepts is a document
  the other can project.
- A custom edge predicate reaches the store. `jj:superseded_by` in an
  `edges:` block resolves to the `jj:supersededBy` the module declares, by
  the same snake_case-to-camelCase rule `x0k:` terms have always used;
  `ingest` used to reject the whole document for it while `check` passed it.
- **`--named superseded` reads your own supersession predicate.** A
  collection whose module declares its own `supersededBy` got that edge
  through `check`, `index`, `ingest` and `--named edges`, and then the
  decision board asked about ours alone and came back empty. It now asks over
  every spelling of the edge the collection was ingested with. `--named
  status` still asks in ours, because its three terms are the folio/v1
  envelope's own.
- `--format json` rows carry paths relative to the corpus root, the way the
  table already did — one convention, so the board you read by eye and the
  board you script are the same board.
- `ingest --vocabulary <dir> --shipped` is no longer refused. The two flags
  were alternatives once; `--vocabulary` is additive now, so naming both is a
  reader saying out loud what is already true.
- One answer reads `1 row`.
- Table rows print paths relative to the corpus root, and `--format json`
  carries a summary of the last reconciliation rather than the whole report
  — `status` prints the rest.

### Guides

- `guides/INTEGRATING.md` describes the tools as they are built. The
  envelope IRIs it prints are the ones the vocabulary declares, and the
  sentences it had outgrown are gone rather than quietly wrong.
- **The build lines say `--release`.** An unoptimized `check` over a real
  documentation tree is 20–46× slower, which is the difference between a CI
  step you can require and one nobody will wait for.
- The guide names the cheapest way in: a module that declares a namespace and
  no classes and no predicates at all, which gives a project its own id
  prefix with the shipped classes and predicates unchanged.

## 0.1.0

First public release: the folio/v1 document format, the `x0k-tangle`
tangler/checker/weaver, the `x0k-folio-cli` query surface, and the
vocabulary modules they read documents against.
